clue.text: Sailor has set back when boom breaks, it's hollow stemmed

indicators.note: set back tells us to turn the sailor's abbreviation round so it reads backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: when the word boom breaks its letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off just as the boom on his yacht snaps, leaving something hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns AB into BA; 'breaks' rearranges BOOM into MBOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant grass is famous for its hollow, jointed canes.

clue.text: Purchase a young animal, fleeced

explanation.surface: A buyer pays for a puppy and gets cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally means buying a puppy; idiomatically, to buy a pup is to be swindled into a bad purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally acquiring a puppy; as an idiom, being cheated in a deal, as a fleeced customer is.

clue.text: Chap to leave a served vegetable

parts.note: a chap is a man
to leave is to get out

explanation.surface: A fellow walks off and leaves a dish of greens behind.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat pea pod is cooked and eaten whole, the French name meaning 'eat all'.

clue.text: Key batsman?

explanation.surface: A question about the most important cricketer in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen go in first; 'Key' also means a device that opens a lock or tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a tool for unlocking things, and in cricket a batsman starting the innings is called this.

clue.text: What may be served in porcelain at meal-time

parts.note: porcelain is china
tea is a light afternoon meal, and the hour at which it is taken

explanation.surface: A picture of a drink poured into fine cups at an afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' is also an afternoon or evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink from the Far East is something offered to guests in cups.

clue.text: Blow for a literary pirate

explanation.surface: A punch thrown by a buccaneer from a storybook.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxing blow with a bent arm; Captain Hook is the villain of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved punch in boxing, and the captain who fights Peter Pan.

clue.text: Sharp decline in air traffic

parts.note: reads as a slump in flight numbers, but describes an aircraft plunging steeply downward, front end first

explanation.surface: A news item about a sudden drop in the number of flights.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used both for an aircraft's steep plunge and for any sudden fall, as in prices.

clue.text: Signs of correctness in insects

explanation.surface: A teacher's marks showing right answers found among the bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks a teacher puts beside right answers, and small bloodsucking parasites loosely called bugs.

clue.text: Salt and vinegar

parts.note: reads as the chip-shop seasoning pair, but describes a chemical salt derived from the acid in vinegar

explanation.surface: The classic British chip seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Vinegar is dilute acetic acid; its salts take this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically, a salt formed from acetic acid, the acid that gives vinegar its sourness.

clue.text: American combination of bets

explanation.surface: A US punter places an accumulator at the bookmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is also a British bet of eleven wagers on four selections.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial term for someone from the US, and an eleven-part multiple wager at a bookmaker's.

clue.text: Dogs race round the cemetery

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are spun about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Greyhounds run laps around a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges DOGSRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a churchyard burial ground, one consecrated to the Lord.

clue.text: Cat provides company in flood

indicators.note: in places the company abbreviation within the flood word

parts.note: a surge is a sudden flood

explanation.surface: A pet cat brings companionship during a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, and a whip used for punishment is called this.

clue.text: Claim money round about end of August

indicators.note: the money word goes round, enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: pence are money
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of August

explanation.surface: Someone asserts their rights to cash around late August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives T from August.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence can be a claim or pretension to something, as in making no pretence to expertise.

clue.text: Lines going to a ship back in port

parts.note: odes are lines of poetry

indicators.note: back turns the pair of a and ship round to read the other way

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the ship abbreviation

explanation.surface: Verses accompany a vessel returning to harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A + SS into SSA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Fiction title?

parts.note: reads as the heading of a novel, but means an invented name, fiction in the sense of a made-up thing, under which an author writes

explanation.surface: A question about the heading of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's assumed name is a fictitious label used in place of the real one.

clue.text: Ground needed for play

explanation.surface: Land is required before the game can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of land, and the storyline every drama requires.

clue.text: Writer of mad revels in midsummer

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters within the month

parts.note: June is the month of midsummer

indicators.note: mad says the letters of revels are crazily jumbled

explanation.surface: An author is behind wild partying on midsummer night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns REVELS into LESVER; 'in' sets it inside JUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: Hit back with a literate composition

indicators.note: composition means the letters are composed, put together, in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone answers an attack with a well-written essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ALITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike in return or take revenge.

clue.text: Incorrect kit means trouble

indicators.note: trouble, as a verb, disturbs the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: Faulty equipment causes a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges KITMEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong, in error.

clue.text: Chap following terrible strain becomes acerbic

indicators.note: following places the chap after the jumbled letters
terrible signals that strain is badly mangled into another order

parts.note: a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A man becomes sour-tempered after enduring awful stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STRAIN into ASTRIN; 'following' puts GENT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, biting, harsh in tone.

clue.text: Made a move to train as a mechanic

indicators.note: made a move says the letters shift position into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone took steps to qualify as a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a move' rearranges TRAINAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker or craftsman; mechanic in the old sense of a manual tradesman.

clue.text: He comes from Constantinople — or Istanbul if you prefer

indicators.note: comes from says the man's name sits inside the city's name, emerging from it

explanation.surface: A man hails from the old city on the Bosphorus, by whichever name.
explanation.walkthrough: The name also sits inside 'Istanbul', so either city name supplies it; 'He' is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, short for Stanley, so a male person, he.

clue.text: County of broad vistas?

parts.note: reads as a place with wide views, but points to the English county famous for its Broads, a network of shallow lakes

explanation.surface: A question about an area with wide views.
explanation.walkthrough: The Broads are lakes and waterways in East Anglia, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This East Anglian shire holds most of the Broads, a lake district of wide flat landscapes.

clue.text: Soldier returns to scene of mutiny and neglect

indicators.note: returns reverses the soldier abbreviation so it reads upward in this down light

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the Nore, an anchorage in the Thames estuary, saw a famous naval mutiny in 1797

explanation.surface: A soldier goes back to where a rebellion happened and is careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GI into IG.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to, disregard.

clue.text: Became fond of and acquired tailless tom

parts.note: acquired means took

indicators.note: tailless cuts the final letter off the tom

explanation.surface: Someone warmed to a stray male cat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' turns TOM into TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Took a liking to, as in 'she took to him at once'.

clue.text: Work overtime to produce a show

indicators.note: over in a down answer places work above time

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Putting in extra hours to stage a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' splits into 'over' + 'time': OP over ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic work set to music and staged as a performance.

clue.text: He does his running on the quiet

definitions.text: He does his running on the quiet

parts.words: He does his running on the quiet
parts.note: reads as a discreet jogger, but describes someone running contraband secretly, as in gun-running or rum-running

explanation.surface: A man who likes to jog without anyone noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who brings goods in illegally covertly ferries, or runs, them.

clue.text: They may part with a smile

definitions.text: They may part with a smile

parts.words: They may part with a smile
parts.note: reads as people saying goodbye cheerfully, but describes the parts of the mouth that open when grinning

explanation.surface: Friends who separate on good terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth's fleshy edges open when someone grins.

clue.text: Dodges past the doorkeeper a telltale offence

parts.note: a sneak is a telltale, one who informs
a sin is an offence

explanation.surface: A gossip slips by the porter, a wrong in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Enters furtively, getting in without being seen by the person on the door.

clue.text: Starchy food dad is about to turn to

indicators.note: is about means dad surrounds the turned piece

parts.note: pa is dad

indicators.note: turn reverses the first little word to so it reads the other way

explanation.surface: Father is going to switch to a carbohydrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes the first 'to' into OT, which PA goes about; the second 'to' is added as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber rich in starch.

clue.text: Order cattle by the head

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Arranging the herd according to the lead animal.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT (cattle) and NESS (a headland) are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness, being in good order.

clue.text: Ornament venerable monk put on head of knife

annotationWithheld.why: 'Ornament venerable monk put on head of knife': BEDE (venerable monk) + K (head of knife) leaves the C of BEDECK unaccounted for; no word supplies it and no search found the clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Ornament venerable monk put on head of knife
